contract: acquire(unlabeled_geometries, observations, budget)->unused indices; fit(observations)->object with potential(atomic_numbers, coordinates_angstrom)->(energy_ev, forces_ev_angstrom). Eight precomputed quantum-label queries from12 source acquisition geometries in the bounded pilot;14 evaluation geometries hold out entire ligand groups. Score force RMSE/(1 eV/Angstrom) + molecule-centered relative-energy RMSE/(1 eV) on source-group holdouts. Independent finite differences check force/energy consistency, rigid-motion symmetries, net force/torque; short evaluator-controlled trajectories check numerical stability. All units are explicit and a test fixture never substitutes for SPICE.
notes: Independently implemented SCIEL adaptation. Source bundles are required except the specified PFHub and Cantera simulations; no generated replacement data. See docs/MATERIALS_EXPANSION.md for provenance, exact setup blockers and validation scope.
protocol_description: Locally authored implementation of the cited scientific task. Source data, generated mathematical instances, reference checks and adaptations are specified below; unit-test fixtures do not establish a benchmark reproduction.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Learn molecular energies and forces with limited expensive quantum-chemical labels.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Accurate molecular potentials can make physically informed molecular simulation less costly.
science_relevance.reason: SPICE is a dataset paper. The inspected active-learning ANI study (Less is more: sampling chemical space with active learning) pursues transferable molecular potentials, but the current eight-query pilot has only twelve acquisition and fourteen evaluation geometries. This review did not establish that this restricted pilot preserves that substantive research objective rather than primarily testing an acquisition interface; no transferable-potential result follows from the pilot. No qualifying primary-goal evidence is established for this local task in this review; this is not a finding that the broader subject is unimportant.
science_relevance.verification_basis: Local task contract and cited source purpose reviewed; background or benchmark citations were not promoted to primary-problem evidence.
science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
